referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 2 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 19 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 7 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 12 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

NRSA benthic macroinvertebrate multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. EPA's Wadeable Streams Assessment MMI of six metrics scored per NARS-9 region, the same index in every survey cycle; EPA's own condition benchmarks are the published criterion it can be scored against.
Total benthic taxa richness; higher is better.

config.caveat: Specific conductance carries natural carbonate geology as well as disturbance: a pristine stream in a calcareous valley can score low on this curve.
config.notes: Specific conductance; higher indicates ionic disturbance (worse).
Total nitrogen; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse). The total fraction, reported in every NRSA cycle, and the fraction published nitrogen criteria are written against.
Total phosphorus; higher indicates nutrient enrichment (worse).

NRSA fish multimetric index (0 to 100); higher is better. Eight metrics per NARS-9 region, several adjusted for watershed area, scored from an electrofishing sample; sites sampled by seining carry no index.
Percent of native fish individuals classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is worse. Dominance by tolerant fish is a standard multimetric-index component of disturbance.
Large woody debris volume per 100 m; higher is better.

config.caveat: Base-flow index is set largely by hydrogeology: a naturally flashy till catchment reads low on this curve without being degraded.
config.notes: Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. Moderate confidence: hydrogeology sets the baseline, so a naturally flashy till catchment reads low without being degraded (see the natural-context criterion below). Scored because flow alteration and withdrawal also move it.

config.caveat: Wetland cover follows terrain: a steep watershed that never held wetland reads low on this curve without being degraded.
config.notes: Watershed wetland (%), woody plus herbaceous, both classes required; wetlands store surface water and attenuate flow peaks. EASI scores Surface water storage on the same sum (method watershed-wetland-extent).
Percent fast-water (riffle/run) habitat; more generally better for many biota. Ecoregion-dependent.
